resolved_conflicts.explanation: The state's National Register page gives 1923 and the Maine Forestry Service map is dated 1923. Maine Memory gives 1920 without a basis. We use 1923 and flag 1920.
The state's page gives 47 feet (the figure used here, 14.3 m). A visitor listing for the trails gives 55 feet. Not resolved; a call to the town or the state preservation office would settle it.
The state page shows a date listed of December 29, 2025, but its text says the tower is eligible for listing. We record the listing date as the page's stated date and flag the wording.

notes_for_editor: The tower is described as standing with its cab in place (FFLA lists no asterisk). Open conflicts: build year 1920 (Maine Memory) versus 1923 (state page and map); height 47 ft (state page) versus 55 ft (trail listing); and the National Register listing date versus the page's eligible wording. A Facebook post by the FFLA Maine chapter says it is now on the National Register; Facebook could not be read, so it is not cited. The Maine Preservation Most Endangered list was not read directly; the Maine Memory page reports it without a year. Last fire-observation use 1967 comes from the state's period of significance, not a staffing record, so no last watchman is named.
